memory_verse.label: Memory Verse
memory_verse.text: “But God said to him, ‘You fool! This very night your soul will be required of you; then whose will those things be which you have provided?’ So is he who lays up treasure for himself, and is not rich toward God.”— Luke 12:20–21

devotion.label: Insight / Reflection
devotion.text:
A person who strives only for personal gain may appear successful, but in reality, he is heading toward great loss. Heaven’s accounting system is the opposite of the world’s. What we lose for God is never a loss; it becomes eternal gain. Yet in today’s world, many people live self-centered lives, thinking only about their own comfort, security, and honor.
On the path of faith, there is one attitude we must firmly reject  self-glory (pride). In a parable, Jesus spoke of a rich man whose land produced abundantly. Having no room to store his crops, he said to himself, “I will tear down my barns and build bigger ones. I will store all my grain there. Then I will say to my soul, ‘You have many goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, and be merry.’”
This rich man was completely self-focused. His words were filled with “I,” “my,” and “mine.” He trusted in his wealth but did not look to the God who gave him life. His plans were centered only on his own pleasure and security. God’s response is a solemn warning to us: “You fool! This night your soul will be required of you.”
To live forgetting God while exalting oneself is spiritual foolishness. A true spiritual believer must immediately reject this self-centered mindset. In the midst of challenges, instead of focusing only on what we possess or lack, we must place our full trust in God and walk in humility. When we surrender every part of our lives to Him, we discover true and lasting success.

quote.label: Today's Quote
quote.text: “He who loses himself gains everything; he who humbles himself shall be exalted.”

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Heavenly Father, grant us grace to reject pride and selfishness in our lives. Help us not to depend on wealth or intellect, but to live with humble hearts before You. Be our true source and guide us to do what is pleasing in Your sight. Amen.

conclusion.label: A Word to You
text: At the end of life, the wealth you gathered will question you. But even the smallest service you did for God will receive eternal reward. The one who loses self and gains Christ is the true victor.
